name: Caribou
long_description:
Going global is now the norm. But the moment you set up an entity in another country, you inherit a tax and legal mess that compounds with every hire and every invoice. 

For example, one jurisdiction has to be profitable, cash has to move between entities compliantly, and every cross-border decision has to be audit-ready, which today means a different law firm in each country, a tax advisor on top of that, and you coordinating the chaos.

The real expertise is locked up inside the Big Four. The world's largest companies pay millions a year for access. Everyone else gets selective coverage and hefty legal bills to half-solve the problem.

Caribou is the first autonomous tax firm. No lengthy workshops, no months of back-and-fort; connect your finance and HR systems and we graph your business — every entity, process, and employee — into a model we call the Atlas. 

From there we check transfer pricing, surface legal risks you didn't know you had, maximise your R&D credits, and monitor for accidental taxes as your shape changes.

And we don't just hand you a report. We speak to your accountants, draft the legal agreements, and implement the fix ourselves. We've turned an 
eight-week engagement into three hours.

Why work with three firms when one does the job?

We're already working with fast-growing companies like Butternut Box, OpenFX, Encord, Vertice, Omnea, and Hadrian - we've saved them hundreds of thousands on legal fees and surprise tax bills.
one_liner: The autonomous tax firm

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer:
From international banking, to international taxes.\
\
Caribou was formerly rebank (W19). rebank was the first open banking product for global businesses. We integrated banks across Europe & the US, allowed you to send money globally, and monitor your financial metrics from one dashboard.

\
Building rebank taught us that companies were going global earlier, and law/accounting firms couldn’t keep up with their cross-border needs. That insight led us to pivot to Caribou in 2024.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
The way startups scale has gone global. Even the smallest teams now operate across borders—with a Delaware C-Corp, a UK subsidiary, and contractors in three countries. But the tax system hasn’t kept up. Every multinational, no matter how small, is legally required to follow _transfer pricing_ rules—complex regulations designed for giants like Google and Apple.

That means founders suddenly have to deal with one of the most complicated areas of tax, law, and accounting: proving that the way their entities share profits, people, and IP is fair and compliant. Getting it wrong can cost them everything—from lost R&D credits and double taxation to failed funding rounds and audits they can’t afford.

Until now, there’s been no solution for this. Big Four firms charge six figures for what early-stage startups need to do, while accountants and lawyers are guessing—or skipping it entirely. We saw founders “flying blind” and leaving huge amounts of cash on the table, not because they didn’t care, but because the system wasn’t built for them.

Caribou changes that. We automate the hardest parts of transfer pricing by collecting and structuring messy business context with AI. What used to take consultants months now takes minutes, and with greater accuracy.

We’re solving this because global ambitions shouldn’t be punished by complexity. Caribou makes international tax compliance simple, affordable, and scalable—so ambitious startups can grow like multinationals, without the pain of becoming one.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
To build the first autonomous tax firm.

For global to feel as frictionless as local.

launches.body:
A year and a half ago, we launched [Firstbase Agent](https://www.firstbase.io/agent) —  our all-in-one state compliance solution for startups. You appoint Firstbase as your registered agent in every state where you operate or have employees, and we receive and view notices from the government, give you reminders about compliance events, and monitor your compliance status in each state, file annual reports, BOI reports, and franchise taxes. We will also help you register and maintain your payroll accounts in any state where you want to hire any employee — this way, you can avoid paying extremely high EOR fees (often around \~$700/employee/month) and instead hire an employee through your own entity. And, of course, we help you fulfill the legal obligation of having a registered agent in every state where you operate. \
\
One huge difference between us and other state compliance providers is that we actually own and operate our own entities in all 50 states as a licensed commercial registered agent. So we have direct contact with the state and don’t have to rely on any third parties for anything.

Why it’s important: to give an example, if you hire an employee in a new state and need payroll accounts, your payroll tax registration partner will typically work with a network of registered agents in different states and won’t really have control over anything. They’ll often need that third party to sign off on forms, which slows things down and often leads to operational nightmares.

Now, almost 15,000 companies are using Firstbase Agent, and we have decided to do something nice and give part of the functionality **_free of charge_**.

**TL;DR -** When buying a home abroad, Ruffo lets buyers complete the required documents 100% online instead of having to get on a plane, go to a foreign consulate, or hire a foreign attorney.

🙄 **The problem**

When purchasing real estate abroad, signing transaction documents is a huge pain. You either get on a plane to sign in person, take your chances going through a maddening DMV-like experience at the nearest consulate, or pay thousands of dollars to (often questionable) foreign attorneys for signing in your name.

The risks, hassles, and costs of today’s cross-border document completion process drives many buyers to abandon their purchase halfway through, and forces many other would-be buyers to hold back. On top of stifling the homeownership dreams of buyers, today’s process also costs home sellers, real estate agents and mortgage lenders millions of dollars in lost sales every year.

![](https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/FpPiykbH8NQkTX3KxSy3oAlLOemXqafh-x66kcjUbyD_pEjzWMJlXEP52n0JR8RdR7bmcO9piJm_DJTlNu-qKSdV3UM1IImfwNaMq1gxl1gbA9tY4sS_hcgzrUztnA759US0RIXp9_2I1Rp4o7clYK0)

We allow buyers to complete, sign and notarize foreign transaction documents from their computer or mobile phone in just minutes. Ruffo generates the relevant transaction documents and connects the buyer to a notary in the U.S. to sign and notarize online. Ruffo then obtains the required government certifications to ensure that the document is legally valid in the foreign country where it will be used. The end result is a seamless foreign document generation and signature experience that saves the buyer time and money, while helping home sellers, real estate agents and mortgage lenders close more sales in less time.

launches.title: Gerri 2.0 - The AI Agent for Contracts from Common Paper
launches.tagline: Put your redlines on autopilot
launches.body:
Most AI contract tools are built to support a single lawyer working within Word. [Gerri is built for everyone with a stake in getting a deal signed.](https://www.getgerri.ai/) 

2 minute intro:[ youtube.com/watch?v=QL4nIETkZnY](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QL4nIETkZnY) 

3 minute demo:[ loom.com/share/ac7906243ce340159797af888488cb6b](https://www.loom.com/share/ac7906243ce340159797af888488cb6b)

**Background:**

More than 10,000 companies have used Common Paper to close deals over the past few years. While the standards have helped, we keep hearing how painful the redline process is. The root cause is that contract negotiation is a team sport, but most tools are built for one player.

Most teams end up in one of two camps:

* Every redline goes to the attorney, which is expensive and slows deals down
* Redlines get triaged first, usually by someone in sales or ops, and contracts are one of 10 things they have on their plate

What's missing is a system where AI does the first read, loops in the right people when needed, and pulls all of their feedback into a new draft that can be sent back to the other side. 

That's Gerri.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99518&key=user_uploads/71220/c7e0519b-5c7b-46d2-8456-3ecbb0a4b5b4)


**How it works:**

Contracts get into Gerri three ways: upload, forwarded email, or direct inbox scanning. From there:

* Gerri reads every redline against your playbook and automatically accepts, rejects, or counterproposes anything it can handle
* Anything outside the playbook gets routed to the right person. That might be legal for indemnity questions, finance for payment terms, VP of Sales for commercial terms, etc.
* Every AI decision cites the specific playbook rule behind it; every human override is logged
* Gerri edits the Word doc directly and can add comments in your name, explaining the reasoning to the other side

Gerri typically reviews contracts before you even know they've arrived. You'll open your inbox, see a contract, and find it's already been handled.

**What's new in 2.0:**

* 10X faster processing engine. 90% of contracts reviewed in under 3 minutes.
* Any contract type: your paper, their paper, standard or custom agreements
* Personality Settings: set custom instructions that guide Gerri's behavior across all contracts, without editing individual playbook rules
* Template Improvement: Gerri analyzes your negotiation history and suggests changes to your outgoing templates that proactively reduce future redlines. The more you use it, the smarter your paper gets.
* Optional attorney review add-on: flat fee, 4-hour turnaround guarantee, for when you need a human in the loop
* Available as a standalone product at [getgerri.ai](http://getgerri.ai)  - No other Common Paper subscription required

launches.tagline: Get your contracts reviewed before you even realize they’re in your inbox
launches.body:
We’re Jake and Ben, co-founders of Common Paper.  We just launched Gerri, the AI agent for redlines. [Try it out here and get three contracts reviewed for free](https://commonpaper.com/product/ai-agent).

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QL4nIETkZnY

## Problem

Common Paper started by creating [standard agreements](https://commonpaper.com/standards/) that have been signed by more than 10,000 companies and used to close more than $100 million dollars in deals. We also make contract management software for customizing, signing, and tracking agreements with customers and partners.

As companies scale, more and more of their sales teams’ time is spent dealing with contract redlines from their customers.  After talking seeing the problem close up at countless companies, we found that most folks fall into one of two camps:

* Every contract redline gets sent to their attorney, which is expensive and adds delays
* Nothing gets sent to the attorney, and the founder, sales, ops, or other non-lawyer handles all redlines. This creates a significant risk when they don’t know what they don’t know about risks in contracts

A better approach is to have AI do a first read of each contract and then triage the redlines so that as much as possible is handled automatically, and then if anything remains, assign it to the right person. That’s what we built with Gerri.

## Solution

There are three ways contracts get into Gerri:

* Upload
* Forward an email with attachment
* Have Gerri scan your team’s inboxes for redlined contracts and automatically review them as they come in

Once Gerri gets a contract, it compares it to your playbook, which contains rules about what you will and won’t accept, how you respond to asks, comments to leave in the doc, etc. Gerri includes a demo playbook to help you get started, and you can chat or answer questions to have Gerri help you generate your own custom rules.

Gerri then either

* Responds with a clean contract that’s ready to send back to the other side.  Gerri automatically accepts, rejects, counter-proposes, and leaves comments for the other side.  
* Flags which redlines can’t be handled automatically, and notifies the right people for them to weigh in. For example, it might be your lawyer for indemnity issues, CS lead for renewal terms, and IT for special security procedures/certifications.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94771&key=user_uploads/71220/c61e5a05-75a4-4f95-a66d-cf4f618bb057)

Each time a human weighs in, they can make a decision for just this one case or have Gerri generate a rule to handle this decision going forward. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94771&key=user_uploads/71220/a1877eb9-5798-4ba5-8b31-eac429cd02b1)

The end result is your contracts get reviewed before you even realize they’re in your inbox, and deals close faster.

TLDR: If you want to close deals faster/shorten your sales cycles with standardized contracts and a platform that helps eliminate back and forth, [we’d love for you to try us out](https://commonpaper.com/)!

# Background

We (Jake and Ben) met while working together at a BI startup called RJMetrics. Jake was a co-founder, and Ben was an engineering leader. At that job and others, we were incredibly **frustrated by contract negotiation**. The process was filled with:

* **⏳ Unpredictable delays**
* **💰 Huge legal bills**
* **🥽 Extremely limited visibility**

We realized that founders and go-to-market teams have many of the same problems with sales that were widespread in startup fundraising before the introduction of the SAFE. Each company has a unique sales or procurement contract (and NDA, DPA, etc).  People argue over whose template to use, and **no matter who wins that argument, one side of the deal has to review and negotiate a new contract for the first time**.

The same basic ideas show up in all contracts about a given type of transaction, but they are expressed totally differently.  As an example, take governing law, one of the simplest terms in most contracts.  These are real examples from four contracts, showing four different ways describe governing law:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=68207&key=user_uploads/71220/b869c8db-5099-478e-855d-b34c5b28bf55)

# Standard Contracts & Structured Data

To solve this, we looked to the SAFE and other widely used contracts for inspiration and created standard, open-source contracts for buying and selling software, including:

* [Design Partner Agreement](https://commonpaper.com/standards/design-partner-agreement/)
* [Mutual NDA](https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/)
* [Terms of Service](https://commonpaper.com/standards/terms-of-service/)
* [Cloud Service Agreement](https://commonpaper.com/standards/cloud-service-agreement/) 
* [Data Processing Agreement](https://commonpaper.com/standards/data-processing-agreement/), [Service Level Agreement](https://commonpaper.com/standards/service-level-agreement/), and more

These contracts have been downloaded by thousands of companies, are created by a committee of attorneys, and are free to use under a Creative Commons license. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=68207&key=user_uploads/71220/bc9fd4c5-56c8-48ed-8ab2-dd024fa5b974)

Using standard contracts reduces back and forth, accelerates sales cycles, and makes it easier for everyone involved to understand what the contracts actually mean.

In addition to the contracts themselves, we’ve built a new kind of [contract management platform](https://commonpaper.com/product/) for startups.  It makes automation, negotiation, and programmatic access to contract data all way faster and easier than ever before. These kinds of tools have traditionally been built for managing unstructured text, and we’ve built Common Paper on top of the **standards and structured data**. 

**⌚ 63% of the deals on our platform close within 24 hours ⏲️**

We also built the [SaaS Agreement Toolkit](https://commonpaper.com/resources/saas-agreement-toolkit), which combines the standard agreements with step by step guides to help founders:

* Choose which contracts to use based on their stage and business model
* Understand the meaning of different terms within the contracts

The toolkit also includes a benchmark report based on the real contracts of more than 150 companies, with data on what positions are most common and how different terms influence the odds of getting your contract signed.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=68207&key=user_uploads/71220/b4ae10b3-d5bf-4439-b700-df82cb92e521)

If you want to shorten your sales cycle, save money, and reduce risk with standardized contracts and a platform that helps eliminate back and forth, [we’d love for you to try us out](https://commonpaper.com/)!

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=73190&key=user_uploads/1369076/99d0dd8f-5228-4ca6-8942-695b81f0605c)

Hello! We’re [**Sona**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sonasulakian/), [**Mariam**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ms-/), and [**Grey**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/greysteil/)—a team of attorneys, security experts, and AI specialists. We’re on a mission to speed up contract negotiation.

### **❌** Problem

* **Sales negotiations get bottlenecked on legal review**. Sales teams must pause deals while they wait for legal teams to redline and finalize customer agreements.
* **Unfriendly terms slip through the cracks**. Legal teams can’t ensure that contracts align with company standards _and_ minimize risk when working under time pressure.
* **Nonstandard language makes understanding your contracts hard.** Lawyers can phrase the same idea in thousands of different ways. At scale, it's difficult to track contract details and negotiation outcomes.

## 💡 Our solution

* **A Word add-in that ensures guidance is available where and when it's needed.** Using the latest large language models, Pincites allows legal teams to build contract playbooks that any internal team can apply consistently within Microsoft Word using our Word add-in. 
* **An AI-powered onboarding flow that turns existing contracts into playbooks.** Simply upload your template, add guidance, and begin redlining. Unlike previous legal tech, manual tagging or model training is unnecessary because Pincites tags clauses based on their semantic meaning.

## **✨** How we help

* **Amplify your legal team’s impact.** Our AI solution surfaces relevant guidance for all teams to quickly review and negotiate contracts using their companies' approved terms. Non-legal teams can securely process contracts, while freeing up legal teams to focus on more critical matters.
* **Flags key risks for review.** Pincites highlights deviations from your standard language and missing clauses in your contracts. We compare each clause to your standard language, providing insights on variations and associated risk levels. We offer guidance for each variation, ensuring you can align on the right language and conveniently access relevant guidance as you work.
* **Standardize contracting language and processes.** Pincites serves as a central place for legal teams to define standard guidance that is then embedded in Microsoft Word for easy access by any internal team.

## 🙏 We’re looking to connect with legal teams! 

* Refer us to your in-house attorneys at [founders@pincites.com](mailto:sona@pincites.com)
* Book a 20 minute demo [here](https://calendly.com/pincites/demo)

Hello! We’re [Chenyu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chenyuli/) and [Sean](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ssafahi/), the team behind [Abel](https://www.tryabel.com/). Abel **answers complex questions across large legal records** made up of many different types of documents. Our mission is to empower attorneys to practice more efficiently, so they can extend representation to more people.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79318&key=user_uploads/363045/d582ce29-dab1-48c8-97ec-23438999b485)

### **tl;dr**

* Attorneys import documents from a variety of sources and formats (PDFs, emails, spreadsheets, docs).
* Abel processes the documents and creates a structured representation of the information contained in them (we call these: “entities”). 
* Attorneys understand the facts with more speed and precision than was previously possible.

### **Problem**

Many legal practice areas - including litigation, M&A, and insurance - routinely deal with large document sets, and attorneys spend many hours reviewing those documents to get the information they need. 

In an age of AI, law firm clients demand both increased efficiency and improved effectiveness. 

Existing technology solutions, like eDiscovery platforms, don’t help attorneys understand the information that exists inside the documents. They’re costly, cumbersome, and their search is difficult to use to pinpoint the relevant information. 

So, attorneys rely on manual document review, which is even more costly, prone to human error, and difficult to get client budget buy-in.

### **Solution**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79318&key=user_uploads/363045/575e7b8c-4331-4a11-b51f-d83c1e0c2535)

Abel allows attorneys to get the depth of manual review at the scale of technology. Attorneys import legal records of a variety of document formats, types, and sizes. 

Abel leverages our proprietary entity extraction to process the documents and uncover a structured representation of the information contained in them. Our extraction pipelines are flexible and can be customized to identify the relevant entities to our customers’ needs, which can include things like: 

* The people involved 
* Clauses in agreements 
* Relevant email threads
* Key legal issues 
* Motions raised at trial
* Key events that occurred

Attorneys use Abel to explore the extracted entities and to examine the relationships between them. This allows us to answer more complex questions with more nuance than existing solutions.

[View our demo.](https://youtu.be/USloYdiY6Pk)

### **Our Asks**

1. If you’re an attorney or responsible for law firm innovation, please reach out to [founders@tryabel.com](mailto:founders@tryabel.com). We’re offering premium onboarding for firms that sign up by May 10th, which includes deploying up to 5 custom entity extraction pipelines. 
2. If you’re on an in-house legal team, we’d love to talk about how we can support both you _and_ your outside counsel. 
3. Please share this post with your networks. Chances are that you know an attorney or two.

launches.body:
Hi YC,

We’re Adam, Andy, and Noah - co-founders of Tower ([withtower.com](https://www.withtower.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=yclaunch&utm_content=launch_page))

## TL;DR

Tower is a collaborative AI diligence workspace. We take your DD checklist and messy data room, organize it, flag what’s missing, and let your team query everything with AI - so you spend time on analysis, not chasing information.

We’re live with AmLaw 50 and Chambers Band 1 law firms, top serial acquirers, and leading commercial real estate diligence teams.

<https://youtu.be/OZn3vZTupGs>

## The Problem

The hardest part of diligence isn’t reviewing documents - it’s collecting the right information. 

Deal teams have no dedicated system for collecting and verifying that disclosures are complete before analysis begins. Instead, they rely on multiple VDRs, Excel trackers, email threads, and one-off AI prompts to figure out what’s been received, what’s missing, and what matters. That process of chasing and structuring information is iterative, time-consuming, and kills deal momentum. 

Most AI tools help teams review documents faster. But you can’t review what you don’t have, and you can’t assess risk in documents you don’t know are missing. 

## The Solution

Tower is the workspace that takes deal teams from first disclosure to answers faster - by fixing collection first, then accelerating review.

**1. Automatically organized data room:** Upload anything, get a fully indexed deal room in minutes. Click any diligence request and see the exact files behind it.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101268&key=user_uploads/1450770/0ac92ee3-6a92-4b0f-8d35-176aa978f693)

**2. Catch red flags and missing files up front:** Missing amendments, unsigned agreements, stale financials, and expired contracts are flagged within seconds of upload, before anyone wastes review time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101268&key=user_uploads/1450770/0e556183-5997-4b8f-b5a1-72fbd4b38bca)

**3. AI document review:** Extract covenants, financial definitions, change-of-control triggers, and rep language across hundreds of documents in one pass. Every answer cited to source.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101268&key=user_uploads/1450770/36914b9b-402a-4ce1-b78e-b1b3bd0341ab)

**4. Smart diligence Q&A:** Every request, every responder, every status, in one live system, synced with the data room. No more "what's the latest tracker?" email threads.

## The Backstory

Our team spent years on the wrong end of messy data rooms - burning weeks organizing and chasing disclosures before real review could begin. We watched deals stall and sour because of it. Tower is the system we wished we had on every one of those deals. 

Noah is a former M&A and tech lawyer at Dentons, where he co-led the AI industry practice and advised top Canadian startups. Andy was an ML quant at a $27B pension fund and founding engineer at NRN Agents. Adam was an early engineer at one of Canada's fastest-growing fintechs, and worked on data science in manufacturing at Apple.

## Our ask

* Warm intros to M&A partners at AmLaw 200 firms, corp dev leads at PE/strategics, and CRE acquisitions teams.
* Working on a deal? Book a demo with us.

Learn more at [withtower.com](https://www.withtower.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=yclaunch&utm_content=launch_page), or reach us directly at [founders@withtower.com](mailto:founders@withtower.com)

launches.tagline: Business leaders have ideas all the time. Overstand lets them validate and act upon them in just a few minutes.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**: [Overstand](https://overstandlabs.com/) is a personal data lab for Execs. We allow business leaders validate their intuitions against their company’s data — with their just their voice, you can go from a raw idea to an evidence-backed answer. They can even see a reproducible step-by-step process and underlying data behind it — all in a few in minutes. Have a look at our [launch video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KrOwutgKsEA).\
\
After working with a bunch of larger companies, we learned something important: some of the most valuable questions are not the ones people plan dashboards for. They're the spontaneous ones, the realizations that you have mid-conversation... the "wait a minute…" moments.

Here’s an example that many of us have encountered at some point: let's say you're talking to a customer, and they say "_you know we've really struggled to figure out how to solve X at our company. Is that something you can help us with?_" They might explain why X is hard, and you'd go back and forth a little.

Then you wonder, at some point — is this just them, or have others said the same thing? Has anyone else on your 200-person GTM team heard of _X_ before? The signal is buried across massive email threads, Gong transcripts, Slack threads, and CRM notes — there’s no way to know quickly.

So this intuition fades. Perhaps you’re able to help that customer in a one-off way, but you don’t see the broader pattern.

We built Overstand to solve for this exact gap — the crevices where data collection has traditionally failed to help you. The spurious thought that you might’ve had.

You articulate your intuition in plain language — "_show me all instances of a customer indicating they're struggling with X._" Overstand builds an entire data pipeline on top of your company's comms + hard data and surfaces the underlying examples that answer your questions — in just a few minutes. From there you can drill down: ask follow-ups to hone in on specific instances, chart the results over time or pull everything into a single context to discuss what was found. You can even action each result individually — sending contextually-crafted emails to each customer who mentioned _X_.

All of this, with just your computer or phone (and you can even do it with your voice — we call it _speech-to-data-pipeline_).

Most enterprise tools are built around questions you already know to ask. Overstand is built around the ones you didn't plan for.

If you're running GTM, CS, or product at a company with real customer volume and this problem sounds familiar — we'd love to talk.

—

Hi everyone, we’re Jackson, Philip, and Ian, and we’re the co-founders of [Parley](http://www.parley.so).

![](https://lh7-us.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdt6N9Q8vNdjiG9xxDpkQcK7DC6o2oJ1pXc5CeFeNpU2jR8qqIb_HbbsvKCgbOuoHmlHJKSF1Y3cnlKz0SCU2BWfICIW3sVsxtv2MV5POsxXUBkkqgYH2Rzq1YRLdcm9rTZf4rLxt6pCFzt6-DOYN-A2yKY?key=bRVaeO2Jsn5Nds8A8Ue9KA)

**📚 The Problem**

It’s no secret that the immigration system in the U.S. is broken. Anyone pursuing a work or immigrant visa will tell you about the difficulties of lottery systems, exorbitant fees, and endless paperwork. 

At Parley, we believe an important piece to fixing this process is **automating work for immigration firms.** For some visa types, a lawyer or legal writer spends several days writing a single application, learning about the most complex and technical professions, collating hundreds of pages of evidence, and synthesizing it all into a cohesive petition. Meanwhile, an applicant eagerly waits for their opportunity. By helping lawyers work better on a daily basis, we hope to accelerate Parley’s speed to impact — reducing the complexity of immigration.

Hey everyone, we’re [Caleb](https://www.linkedin.com/in/caleb-m-harris/) and [Herbie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/herbert-turner-1b511b238/)!

We met almost six years ago while studying computer science at MIT, and have spent the last few months building [&AI](https://www.tryandai.com/) after discovering how much attorney time is spent on tedious and repetitive aspects of patent due diligence.

### **tl;dr**

&AI is a platform that streamlines patent due diligence. By using AI to understand the inventive aspects of patents and automate the creation of work products, we enable attorneys to instantly and comprehensively find prior art, produce robust claim language, invalidate weak patents, and more.

### ❌ The Problem

Imagine a law firm is tasked with determining the strength of a patent or set of patent claims. This is an everyday problem for patent attorneys and could be for anything from a patent application to an IP litigation case. 

To start, the attorneys need to conduct a prior art search. Typically, either:

1. The attorneys meet with an outsourced search provider and give them their claims and features of interest. After a week or two, the provider returns with 5-10 reasonable documents, charging up to $10k.
2. The attorneys manually use boolean keyword searches through databases like Google Patents and decades-old legal research platforms. Over the course of 10-20 billed hours, they have found 5-10 reasonable documents.

In either case, they have already contributed a massive amount of resources to this project without much validation that they are going in the right direction.

With their prior art in hand, the attorneys must evaluate the claims with respect to the art. This involves drafting work products like claim charts, which require several read-throughs of each document to identify and map the relevant language over the course of 20-40 billed hours. By now, the attorneys should have a good idea of the strength of the claims, whether they need to be revised, and whether they may be invalid.

**What if they haven’t found the invalidating art?** They repeat the process. Over and over again, for every patent, for every case. Due diligence can continue almost indefinitely, and it’s only limited by attorney time and client budgets.

### ✅ The Solution

Now, imagine the law firm is using &AI. **Upon receiving the patent or claims, they find the invalidating prior art and export comprehensive claim charts in seconds!** &AI enables both attorneys and inventors to conduct their patent due diligence at a speed, scale, and quality that has never before been possible.

In minutes, we can analyze and compare the inventive aspects of thousands of patents, allowing attorneys to spend less time on tedious work and more time developing their arguments. 

We’ve built our platform to be broadly applicable and easy to use. Users can leverage our AI for patent applications, responses to office actions, and invalidity, with use cases of freedom to operate, infringement, and portfolio analysis coming soon.

### **TLDR**

_FocusBuddy is an AI productivity coach that sits in the background on your computer and speaks to you while you work to help you think clearly, avoid distractions and hold you accountable. Our users converse with the AI over a phone call for 3-4 hours everyday while they’re working_.

### **The Cost of ADHD** 

We’re starting by focusing on people that struggle with ADHD

**People with ADHD consider it the BIGGEST blocker in their life and the PRIMARY cause of their poor grades, missing promotions, and getting fired.**

* 17 million adults and children in the US
* 2-4 more hours wasted every day compared to peers

Beyond ADHD, there are 80 Million people knowledge workers in high income countries that struggle with workplace productivity that FocusBuddy will serve

### **How Focus Buddy helps our user Jeff**

Jeff is a brilliant product engineer who has ADHD. He often struggles to complete work due to his tendency to hyper-focus on details and get distracted by sudden impulses. Here is what Jeff's new workflow looks like since he started using FocusBuddy: 

Jeff calls Focus Buddy first thing in the morning after breakfast. They go over his to-do list together and create a schedule for his day. Jeff then begins his first task - writing a draft PRD. He explains his approach to FocusBuddy and asks for frequent check-ins to keep him on track. 

An hour into drafting, Jeff notices a small discrepancy in a user activity chart. His ADHD brain latches onto this detail, and he spends the next 30 minutes hyper-focusing on it, losing sight of the bigger picture. Just then, FocusBuddy speaks up: "How's it going?" Jeff explains: "He is still figuring out the details on the chart" FocusBuddy detects that Jeff has been hyper-focusing on a detail and helps Jeff realize that he is falling behind on schedule with more important parts of the PRD.

Focus Buddy then works with Jeff to wrap up work on the chart discrepancy and reorganize his schedule to come back to the chart later in the day. They then do a 5-minute meditation to shift his focus away from the discrepancy and ease his mind back onto the main task. At the end of the day, FocusBuddy helps Jeff perform a daily reflection and prepare for his day tomorrow.

Jeff and our other users experience multiple types of interventions by Focus Buddy every single day and attribute their new-found productivity to it.

### **Why Focus Buddy works**

Today, people with ADHD spend hours every day virtually co-working on apps like Focusmate, updating to-do lists, using meditation apps like Calm, and journaling with little success. It is extremely hard to keep these apps updated, they have very little context about you and are unable to proactively provide timely support when needed. 

Focus Buddy is deeply integrated, is seamless to interact with, builds a lot of context over time and is able to leverage this context at critical moments to provide the necessary support.

On top of that, our voice AI infrastructure is revolutionising the way humans and AI interact. we're crafting an entirely new paradigm for fluid, natural conversations that feel as intuitive as talking to another person. Here are some examples:

launches.body:
[**Patent Watch Launch Video**](https://youtu.be/9rLBsb_cX6E)

**Problem**

My co-founder, [**Andreas Stroe**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andreasstroe) (also my brother), was doing research at Philips. He applied for 4 patents while he was there. After spending way too much time talking to the IP team, he realized that they hold 50,000 patents with a team of \~10 people to defend them.

A little background: a **patent costs** around **$50k** to obtain and maintain. $17k is non-negotiable, paid directly in fees. That means their **portfolio costs $850M** to **$2.5B**. The best part is that they, and pretty much every company in the world, rely on Googling competitors and sending salespeople to trade shows to hear about new products that could be infringing. This whole **portfolio** is **making** little to **no revenue.**

I guess you can see why we started building this right away.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94773&key=user_uploads/1250636/63eddfc4-bbda-4f22-b80e-7d4f0f15ced3)

_Can you tell we’re brothers?_

**Solution**

Super simplified to keep it easy to understand:

✅ We let companies upload their patents and get a list of claim charts showing what **products are infringing and how**, in 20 minutes instead of months.

✅ When companies get sued, they can **use us to find counter litigation**, since the person suing them is most likely infringing on some of the patents they hold too.

✅ The most common way to get these cases thrown out of court is by considering a patent invalid. That means there is some proof, like other patents, research papers, or products that existed before your patent was filed. We find all these and **confirm your patents will hold up in court.**

There is more, but you can consider this our “core”.

**Proof**

As you can imagine, pretty much everyone we work with has us under NDA. What I can tell you is that we work with private inventors up to Fortune and Global 500 companies.

**Why now?**

Of course, AI …

But also, the US Patent Office is tightening the rules for challenging patents in its review court. The director is being pickier about which cases get heard, and some evidence no longer counts.

🚨 It’s going to be a lot harder to attack a patent and a lot easier for owners to defend one🚨

**Ask**

If you hold patents and have more applications pending, you can probably use us.

Outside of that, we’d really appreciate intros to:

* Patent attorneys
* IP managers
* Licensing managers
* CTOs or heads of R&D at hardware, biotech, industrial, and large software companies

**TL;DR:** Erinys is building a network of AI-native law firms. Lawyers bring their expertise, judgment, and client relationships. We provide the technology and business infrastructure that lets them launch a new practice or transform an existing one.

<https://youtu.be/96tLvWe4IOM>

\
**The problem**\
Lawyers spend surprisingly little of their time doing work that requires their unique expertise.\
\
Running a practice means finding clients, managing intake, hiring staff, handling billing, overseeing marketing, and keeping the business moving. Small firms burn lawyer hours on it; large firms hire entire teams to manage this. Either way, it kills time or margins.\
\
The legal work itself is still built around lawyers producing everything. Lawyers spend hours turning raw information into research, analysis, and first drafts, even as AI becomes capable of producing much of that work. Existing legal software makes individual tasks faster, but leaves the underlying model unchanged.\
\
We think that model should flip. AI should produce the first pass. Lawyers should direct, review, decide, and advocate.

**How we solve it**\
Erinys provides the infrastructure for lawyers to operate this way from the ground up.\
\
For lawyers starting a practice, we help launch it. For lawyers with an existing practice, we help transition it onto the same model.\
\
Our systems run the business behind the practice while AI assists with fact development, legal research, analysis, and drafting under attorney supervision.\
\
The result is a firm where lawyers spend more time exercising judgment and serving clients, and less time producing routine work or managing the day-to-day mechanics.\
\
One exceptional lawyer can operate with the capabilities that previously required a much larger organization.\
\
**Why us**\
Most legal AI is being built to make the traditional law firm more efficient. We are building the infrastructure for a different kind of law firm, AI-native at its foundation.

Before Erinys, our founding team worked in offensive security, another high-stakes, sensitive, and deeply adversarial environment. We are bringing that security-first mindset to an industry entrusted with its clients’ most sensitive information.
